note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and the worker is based on a single specimen.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparisons with A. ctenopher, A. muricatus, A. pectinatus and A. rastratus have been given under those species. The alate is easily recognized by its exceptionally large compound eyes and ocelli, and is thereby distinguished from the remaining three species, A. sentosus, A. spinulatus and A. tranquillus; the worker is also clearly distinguished by the very long hooked spines of its enteric valve apparatus. Even A. spinulatus, which likewise has slender spines, cannot be confused here, since its mandibular apical tooth is longer and the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is separated from the molar prominence.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity yellow, sparse. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/L1 0.53, Ra/Ri 0.68; in surface view the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is exactly level with the margin of the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 8.40; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, Ra/Ri·Rm 10.40. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 5.10; third apical spur about one third the length of the other two spurs. The midgut–hindgut junction is oblique; the enteric valve seat has a short neck and is dorsolateral in the unopened abdomen; cushion 1 is sclerotized along its whole length, half of it projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other positions, the spines confined to the swollen distal end, the stalk smooth; the spines on the margin of the swollen end number 30–40, the middle of the broader part is inflated and bears a second row of long spines, behind which long and smaller spines are scattered; the cushions of the other positions bear 7–10 extremely slender straight spines, each with a fully reflexed hook at its tip, able to interlock with the spines of the other positions to form a cruciate network; no distinct minute spines were seen on the valve membrane between or outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown, not darker above the ocelli; fontanelle irregularly oval, almost vestigial, much smaller than the ocellus, flat or slightly concave, pale or yellowish brown; central spot oval, flat, almost as large as the fontanelle, slightly paler than the head capsule; postclypeus pale yellowish brown, labrum pale yellow; frontal groove pale yellowish brown, a flat crescent; antennae yellow. Pronotum pale brown, meso- and metanotum pale yellowish brown, transverse sutures almost absent; femora pale yellow, tibiae and tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles pale brown, sternites and ventral spiracles very pale brown, the median part of the sternites and the cerci pale yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli and compound eyes both large and almost touching, the greatest distance less than one quarter of their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.23, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture present in the female and weak in the male. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.53–0.55, Ra/Ri 0.75–0.77; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is distinctly separated from the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 6.10–6.87; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, and the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is longer than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum of moderate width at the constriction, M/W 0.29–0.33. Cephalic pilosity very pale brown, the layer even, with scattered outstanding setae.
